chapter_title: Predicting What Comes Next: Exploring Sequences and Progressions
key_takeaways: A sequence is an ordered list of terms defined explicitly by position n or recursively by previous terms.
The Virahānka-Fibonacci sequence (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ...) originated in India with Virahānka (7th century CE) to analyze poetic meters.
Arithmetic Progressions (APs) grow/decay by adding a constant common difference d (t_n = a + (n-1)d) and plot as straight lines.
Geometric Progressions (GPs) grow/decay by multiplying by a common ratio r (t_n = a r^{n-1}) and plot as non-linear exponential curves.
Practical phenomena like bouncing balls, bacterial growth, and fractal geometry (Sierpiński carpet) follow GP rules.
